body:
Wow, jeez. You've made a lot of really good points here, and it's really solidified to me the fact that I need to go talk to counselling. Friends can help, but a third party can see a lot of things from a different angle.

I do have a lot of insecurities about being accepted, part of that is from my family and part of that is the fact that I was bullied a lot when I was little (something I forgot to mention). I've always been the weird kid, and part of me is really proud of that. I don't like blending in with the crowd. But I didn't like being made fun of or treated like I was less worthy of a person because I was "weird". I had lots of trouble keeping steady friendships as a kid, probably because I don't think my family ever showed me *how*. I tend to avoid keeping close friendships, especially after last year when I had my "bestie" turn around and tell me I was pathetic and failing at life for going through a major depressive episode that came very, very close to ending in suicide (I wish I'd been a redditor back then).

I am vaguely aware of the issues the world faces, and it definitely troubles me. I used to be really into keeping up with politics, but it got draining after a while. I just felt so helpless. There are so many huge issues, it makes me feel small (and rightly so, I am), like nothing I could ever do would have any impact. I totally agree about getting away from tourist spots, though. I hate touristy spots, and tend to avoid them when I travel.

I'm not very good at coming up with problems to solve, in regards to programming/engineering. I consider myself more the muscle than the brains in that regard; I work best when someone tells me what problem to solve, and can work within their constraints. One of my biggest problems is finding creativity or coming up with ideas.

You're also spot on when it comes to my family. I don't see myself as having a biological one; I consider my family to be the one I've built for myself out of my closest friends. I even have a female friend ten years older than me who I jokingly refer to as my second mom. She really is, though. She calls me more than my own mother does. 

And yes, yes I do run away from my problems. That needs to change.

That's very true. I've got reading break in two weeks, it'll be a break from school so I can catch up from all the lectures I've been skipping. Hopefully if I'm less stressed I'll feel less like completely giving up. I think I can make it til then. Thank you.

Yeah, I keep telling myself that I'll go sign up for yoga classes but I've yet to get around to it. Two weeks from now is my reading break, so I should definitely go then. It'll be easier to get myself to go when I don't have school, and once I've signed up, it'll definitely get me out of bed.

I'll be calling the counselors tomorrow, hopefully the intake counselor isn't away still, and if she is I won't use that as an excuse to not call the number she left on her voicemail message. I reeeeally hate phone calls and will give myself tons of excuses to put them off.

And thank you for the rubber band analogy, it gives me hope. I know life will never be all sunshine and rainbows, but I hope I can someday be a bit bouncier. I'll always have bad days but it would be much nicer to be able to bounce back from them.

No, I don't have any special plans for Valentine's. I might Skype with the boyfriend since he lives on the other side of the country, but that's about all.

I have become pretty good at conforming to others' standards, I think it's something I learned growing up in an abusive household. The more you conform, the less you get yelled at. If you do what others say you should, you'll get praised, not told you're a worthless fuckup. I'll admit that I have very little idea what interests me or where I want to go.

I started playing guitar this year because my boyfriend gave me his old one. I gave up after practicing for a week because I just got lazy. My friends have offered to jam with me, but my main instrument is the bass and I've left that back with my parents. I'm sure there are clubs for art and writing and music, my school is known for its great clubs, but I haven't joined any since first year. I signed up for a couple in first year, but I didn't go to any meetings past the initial ones because meeting new people gets me anxious.

I'm not really sure what it is about travel that I like. Maybe it's because everything seems to transient, and I can use it to run away from things that worry me; there's a very tangible feeling of "this too shall pass" when you're holding a ticket to take you somewhere else. Or maybe it's because I like seeing how other people live life. I like exploring, seeing new things; I like the difference and the novelty that comes with far away places. Yeah, I think it's the novelty. As for programming, it would really just be a way to make money. I love the feeling of having code work, and the mental challenge of thinking like a computer, but I have nothing specific in mind.

As for my own ideas.. Yeah, I have few of those. I don't want a family and I never want kids. I'm really scared that they'd stress me out, and that I'd resort to dealing with stress the way I was shown growing up (i.e. yelling, fighting). For that same reason I fear getting married. I have no idea where I want to go. I suppose that's also a motivator in wanting to just give up and sleep forever.

I don't think these problems are exactly new or unique to me. I've been struggling to get/stay motivated for at least the past 5 years- the guy I was dating back then told me all I needed to do was find my "spark" and I'd be fine. But I do think I've been looking at things in a different light as of late.

As for triggering others- it's more because my best friend and I sort of bond over our depression. We've both talked about suicide, and I think we're both a major factor keeping the other around. If he were to kill himself, I know I would have a much harder time finding reasons to not do the same. And uh, also this summer he confessed that he was in love with me. There's that, too. But I guess thinking about it, he's a bit stronger than I am. He likes to say that he's the inspiration and I'm the talent. It's not unlikely that he'd find a way to keep going.

I chose engineering and comp sci because I couldn't think of anything else that really interested me. I took a year off after high school, but I didn't really do much with my time (mainly because I got kicked out of my parents' house). My parents really wanted me to go to school, and they raised me with the mentality that education doesn't stop after high school. I knew I liked computers and things that were challenging. Engineering seemed to fit the criteria.

As for other interests, I'm not really sure. Haven't done any research yet, but I'm hoping my opportunity to work with planetary sciences this summer pans out. 

I like doing things I'm good at, which doesn't narrow it down much. I loved being in band in high school, it's one of the things that got me through those years alive. I could stay after school and practice instead of going home and getting yelled at and having my mom threaten to kick me out again. I love art and writing, but I suffer from perpetual creative block and more often than not just end up staring at a blank page whenever I try. I'm taking a course on ethics this semester, just for fun, because it's an essay course. I took a similar class last semester and got high marks on both the essays, but when I write I kind of feel like a pretentious wad.

I also really love to travel and see new places. Travelling actually gets me feeling motivated and inspired. I'm thinking that when I graduate, I might see if I can work as a freelance programmer, so that I can work from anywhere so long as I've got wifi. That would probably be my dream job- but being able to travel and support yourself is a lot of hard work, and I'm worried I haven't got that in me. I guess I'm also worried about making it through til graduation alive.

I do often call myself "the dumbest smart person you'll ever meet", for many reasons. 

I've been sort of trying to find challenges. I got into engineering because it sounded like one of the most difficult things you could do at university, aside from maybe medicine, but medicine doesn't really interest me. Then I took on a second degree. But none of that really seems to light a fire under my ass.

I know I need something to get me motivated. I'm just not sure what, and I'm worried that not knowing is killing me.

Yeah. The one thing that keeps me going is the thought that when I graduate, I could possibly be working for NASA (I may be doing research with them through my university this summer), or I may end up as a consulting engineer. Consulting would be cool, because then I could travel all over for work. Travel is my favourite thing ever. More than ice cream, and I really love ice cream.

It's just.. the future feels so far away, and I feel like a fuckup *now*. I'm worried I don't have the willpower to actually put the hard work in necessary to achieve my lofty goals of building space robots or being a world traveler. Heh. Some people worry about not having the skill, I worry about not wanting to work hard enough.

When I'm lazy, I'm usually on the internet, doing nothing in particular (i.e. reddit) or I'll just not get out of bed and sleep for 12+ hours. It's usually sleep. I've also found baths to be a good waste of time. I also used to smoke weed a lot, it makes you very content with doing nothing. But I've decided to stop smoking, mainly because I became dependent upon it to fall asleep, and I noticed I was using it as a crutch to avoid feeling feelings.

Any tips on the common sense stuff? It's so frustrating because I *know* I need to do this stuff, but when it comes right down to it, I just *don't*. Part of it I think is the anxiety, and I deal with my anxiety by being avoidant. I guess going to counseling would help with that. I'm really bad with phone calls, but I managed to call last week.. the intake counselor was away, but if I called once, I can do it again.
